# Requirement-to-Concept Trace

| Requirement                                      | Concept                                                           | State/behaviour                                                                                  | Decision                                                              |
| ------------------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| System shall be maintainable and easy to support | Simplicity                                                        | System will only focus on necessary functions.                                                   | Keep the scope small                                                  |
| Manage appointment Status                        | Be able to view and manage the status of an appointment           | If an appointment has been changed then the status will reflect that. E.g. appointment canceled. | Give each appointment a status value and be able to update and check. |
| View Appointment History                         | Store the appointment history of a patient                        | Staff can view the appointment history of a patient when needed.                                 | Each patient will have a list that stores their appointment history.  |
| Manage patient bookings                          | Patients will be able to manage their own bookings.               | If a patient books or cancels an appointment the application will update with that information.  | Create tools to allow patients to place and cancel bookings.          |
| Eliminate duplicate bookings                     | Make it impossible for the program to receive a duplicate booking | If the booking has been booked make it unavailable for anyone else to book it.                   | Create a system that manages what bookings are available.             |
| Display patient information                      | Ability to retrieve the patient information                       | Staff can view information about the patient when needed.                                        | Create a system to return all information about a patient.            |
| View practitioner availability.                  | Practitioners can indicate when they are available.               | When a practitioner updates their availability, the program will reflect that information.       | Create a system for practitioners to manage their timetables.         |

# CRC Cards

## Patient

| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Stores and displays information about the Patient. E.g. Name, Age, Date of Birth. | Practitioner  |
| Allows patients to update information.                                            | Appointment   |

## Practitioner

| Responsibilities                                                                            | Collaborators |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Stores and can display information about the Practitioner. E.g. Name, Age, and Availability | Patient       |
| Allows the program to know when the Practitioner is available.                              | Appointment   |

## Appointment

| Responsibilities                                                     | Collaborators |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------- |
| Allows patients and staff to view available and booked appointments. | Practitioner  |
| Allows staff to change the appointment status.                       | Patient       |

# Design Rationale

Explain class selection, responsibility allocation and key relationships.

Practitioner, Appointment and Patient would be the three main classes for this program. An additional class that could be added is the clinic class. This class only would need to be added if the program was expanded to support multiple clinics. The practitioner and patient classes would both be associates of the appointment class. This is because appointments would need a patient and a practitioner needed to be an appointment. Each appointment would only have 1 practitioner and 1 patient.

# Reflection

The hardest modeling decision was figuring out what information is needed for each class. When designing the class I would constantly overlook what information should be given to the patient class. An example of information I overlooked was a value to store the patient phone number. AI over-designed by suggesting functionality that is outside of the scope of the application. The evidence that supported my final choices were what I could figure out was needed based on the brief provided .
